wire_scope_definitions.durable_event: Valid Event Envelope kind for persisted canonical history and reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.actor_private_event: Persisted actor-private/account-data event; not shared Realm history and not Realm reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.ephemeral_event: Transient sync/federation/app signal; MUST NOT be persisted as durable Event Envelope history.

admission_class_definitions.self_authored_proof: Admitted by a proof bound to the subject principal's identity: either the subject's DID-bound signature / proof of possession, or a currently valid delegated-control proof whose authorization_ref is bound by the subject DID Document. Reducer MUST verify actor == subject, executed_by/authorization_ref when delegated, a fresh replay-protected proof, and that the accepted-at delegation purpose/scope explicitly covers the target event kind, resource and operation; mere presence of a DID-bound delegation is never sufficient. No Realm capability grant is consulted. Fail-closed: missing, stale, unbound, purpose-inapplicable or scope-inapplicable proof MUST be rejected.
admission_class_definitions.did_root_anchor: Admitted only by the closed identity-root anchor verifier. v1 permits this class for a self-principal PCR genesis ak.realm.create bound to entry 0 through one critical did_inception ref, and for B-model ak.device.reanchor bound to the accepted registry head through one critical did_recovery_anchor ref. This verifier is the sole exception to generic Event verification_method-controller equality: verification_method MUST instead equal an active controller-proof verification method from the referenced entry, and the verifier validates it against the accepted did:webvh history/update authority without rewriting its did:key controller to actor_id. Root/update authority MUST NOT authorize any other Event kind. Batch shape, DID history, active update authority, full frontier CAS and conflict-slot checks remain mandatory.
admission_class_definitions.delegated_pcr_genesis: Admitted only for a principal_control ak.realm.create with no did_inception ref and with both executed_by and authorization_ref. The verifier MUST prove actor_id is a managed Agent or explicitly organization-governed principal, resolve authorization_ref in that actor DID's accepted ArkretPrincipalControlRealm/controller delegation, require realm_id and payload.object.id to equal the delegated PCR binding, require proof.verification_method to resolve to executed_by or its current authorized device, and reject self-principal or generic realm.create-capability substitution. This class never authorizes the following device authorize slot by itself.
admission_class_definitions.deny: Explicit fail-closed admission branch. Selection always rejects the Event as failed_precondition/schema_violation and MUST NOT consult capabilities or alternate proof paths.
admission_class_definitions.conditional: Admission is selected from the event row's closed admission_variants. Receivers evaluate every non-otherwise predicate using admission_predicate_contract: exactly one match selects that variant, more than one match is fail-closed, and zero matches selects the single final otherwise variant. The otherwise branch is a fallback and is not counted as a simultaneously matching predicate. Each selected variant applies its own admission class and capabilities.
admission_class_definitions.service_attested: Written by a protocol service component (Auth/Gate server, Events node, applet host, agent runtime) under its service-ID attestation as part of operating the protocol. Reducer MUST verify the issuing service's authority and its binding to the subject/scope; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.crypto_verifiable: Admitted by cryptographic verification of the payload against group/key state (MLS epoch, key material, franking) and its policy preconditions. Reducer MUST verify the cryptographic binding; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.capability_gated: Gated by one or more named capability actions listed in admission_capabilities. Reducer MUST verify the actor holds a matching action grant per capability-action-registry. Fail-closed.

admission_predicate_contract.selector_semantics: All selector fields in one non-otherwise when object are ANDed. payload_path is relative to Event.payload; const uses exact JSON value equality, while not_const matches inequality or an absent path. top_level_fields_present requires every listed Event Envelope field. ref_* selectors evaluate Event.refs after schema validation. Unknown selectors, missing companion selectors, multiple matching non-otherwise variants, or evaluation errors are fail-closed.

registry_rules: Standard ak.* effect kinds MUST appear in this registry when used by a DataEvent effect, Control Move effect, or Event Envelope payload router.

Events API, Sync durable history, Federation, and canonical reducers MUST accept only active entries with wire_scope=durable_event unless an implementation profile explicitly defines a private channel for actor_private_event.
Entries with wire_scope=ephemeral_event MUST be carried only on ephemeral channels and MUST NOT advance Seal coverage, governance state_root, or reducer state.

Entries with wire_scope=actor_private_event MAY be persisted in encrypted account data or an actor-private stream, but MUST NOT be inserted into shared Realm data-plane history or control-plane Seal history.

Every active lifecycle event kind MUST declare lifecycle_modality. Use reversible for a reversible lifecycle facet or either member of an archive/restore pair, and terminal for an irreversible transition that cannot be restored. Reducers and SDKs MUST NOT infer modality from event-kind spelling or the presence of a sibling event.

Every active reducer-input durable kind MUST declare plane, sealed, and a complete machine-readable cell contract. A single-target kind MAY use the legacy cell_family/cell_subject/lattice/bottom shorthand. cell_writes[] is the general authority and is REQUIRED for multi-target kinds; each entry declares cell_family, cell_subject, lattice, bottom, and optional initial_value. The generator materializes the single-target shorthand when cell_writes[] has one entry. cell_family is a stable ak.component.*.v<n> URI; cell_subject is null, an envelope/payload field path, a coalesce descriptor, or a composite descriptor. plane MUST be data or control; sealed is a boolean and MUST be true iff plane=control. plane/sealed are the machine-readable authority for DataEvent versus Control Move routing and plane_cross_write validation; payload prose is explanatory. bottom is reject, expose, or inert; inert MUST be used when the lattice cannot produce Bottom. initial_value declares the value the cas_register reports before any effect has been applied; declaring `initial_value="__unset__"` combined with `head_eq:"__unset__"` implements singleton-once-set cells.

Protocol-singleton cells MAY take their genesis value from a create payload, but every subsequent write MUST use a registered event_kind. ak.component.notary.v1 is canonically defined in zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 6.5; its genesis value comes from ak.realm.create and subsequent writes use ak.realm.notary.

Lattice MUST be one of the fully specified core types: or_set, mv_register, cas_register, fsm, counter, ordered_log. A new lattice type cannot become active until its join, bottom, op schema, profile gate, and conformance vectors are all registered.

State convergence is defined by CBA: DataEvent effects are locally accepted against seal_ref, Control Move effects are finalized by Seals, and per-cell Lattice join remains deterministic. Event Envelope routing fields MUST NOT be used as ordering authority.

Every active durable reducer-input event_kind MUST have a machine-readable admission source: either at least one capability action targets it (capability_action_registry.target_event_kinds), or it declares an admission class from admission_class_definitions. capability_gated events MUST list the authorizing action(s) in admission_capabilities. Enforced by lint_artifacts.py; no active durable reducer-input event may lack an admission source (fail-closed).

A conditional admission MUST use only selectors defined by admission_predicate_contract. All non-otherwise predicates are evaluated independently; exactly one match selects its branch, zero matches selects the final otherwise branch, and multiple matches fail closed. otherwise is never evaluated as an ordinary predicate.

payload_schema_contract.validation_rule: Every active standard ak.* event kind MUST be validated by the Event Envelope schema and one payload class selected by kind. Unknown standard kind, unmatched active kind, or payload class failure is schema_violation before reducer execution.
payload_schema_contract.non_critical_extension_rule: Unknown non-critical payload fields are preserved in canonical bytes and MAY be ignored by reducers. Unknown critical payload semantics MUST be declared in Event.requirements.critical_extensions and fail closed when unsupported.

event_kinds.payload: Organization-authorized Realm relationship statement or revocation

Typed Realm link graph edge. link_kind declares governance / discoverability / import-export / confidential-extension semantics; it is never generic parent/child containment and never implicitly propagates membership, capabilities, history, E2EE keys, retention, or federation policy.
Realm preview / peek policy for directory card, stripped state, history stub, and plaintext history snippet projections

Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer. payload = {realm_id, strand_id}; reducer projects payload.strand_id into the Realm projection default_strand_id (single authoritative pointer; avoids multi-default dirty state). Reducer MUST verify the referenced strand_id already exists in this Realm (a projected, non-tombstoned Strand); a dangling reference MUST be rejected with failed_precondition. Strand-side is_default is a derived marker (strand_id == realm.default_strand_id), never independent storage; clients discover the default Strand deterministically from the Realm projection default_strand_id or the Strand projection is_default, NOT from any UUID-reuse implementation detail. Authorization is the standard Realm-admin gate (hold ak.realm.admin, or the same-name action ak.realm.set_default_strand).
CAS rotation of the per-Realm notary authority. The current notary must finalize the Move; concurrent rotations join to Bottom and require recovery.
Profile-gated transition from the Realm's current digest suite to a stronger active suite, bound to a transition snapshot and dual-root Seal under ak.profile.hash_transition.v1.
Enabled Realm policy components set. Payload MUST carry monotonic policy_revision; reducer rejects rollback or gaps and policy_frontier_digest MUST cover policy_revision.

Constraints on member delivery_binding: which binding_source values are admissible, which recipient services are allowed, which endorsers are required, whether DID Document fallback / unroutable membership are permitted, who may sign rebind. Governs reducer acceptance of ak.member.state{membership=join}.delivery_binding (see governance/join-policy.md §5.1).
Realm read receipt disclosure policy (disclosure / visibility / scope_overrides_allowed / receipt_compliance_opt_in); see zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §2.5 for the closed compliance opt-in object
Realm moderation policy (blocklists, allowlists, content filters)
Plaintext-visible services declaration outside E2EE boundary
Per-parent inheritance policy; one entry per source Realm
Realm tombstone lifecycle facet (terminal pointer to successor)
Realm destroy lifecycle facet (terminal decommission marker)
Circle create (intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary). Initializes independent MLS group and epoch-0 governance binding only when encryption_profile=mls_rfc9420. See zh/models/circle.md §3, §5.

Full ak.schema.agent_sidecar.v1 object. Accepted only inside the atomic ak.self.agent.sidecar.command.ensure aggregate after its reducer-derived backing Circle exists. The canonical Event materializes backing_circle_id and is stamped into that Circle effective scope; raw ensure callers cannot supply it. See zh/models/sidecar.md §2-§5.
Circle patch (ak.patch.v1 with path NOT containing realm_id / encryption_profile). Modifies title / summary / display / directory_visibility / join_rule / history_visibility.
Circle tombstone (terminal). Triggers lifecycle cascade per zh/models/circle.md §9.2.

Circle membership state. Uses the same membership_state enum as ak.member.state (invite/join/knock/leave/ban), scoped to a Circle. Reducer MUST first validate the target actor is a parent Realm `join` member, otherwise failed_precondition reason=circle_member_must_be_realm_member. See zh/models/circle.md §9.1.

Reducer-derived: Circle sub-seal commits opaque sub_seal_head_digest to the Realm Seal stream at the Circle's profile-defined cadence. MUST use time-based ticks + empty-batch commitment to avoid leaking activity frequency. See zh/models/circle.md §10.2.

Issuer-signed endorsement that a subject DID (typically an agent / service / hosted actor) is accountable_principal_ids the issuer for a declared scope (employment / contracted_service / agent_operator / etc.). Required to verify `Actor Profile.accountable_principal_ids[]` entries; reducer strips unverified DIDs from accountable_principal_ids. See zh/models/actor.md §3.3.1. expires_at is optional; absent means non-expiring, governed by grant_status revocation and controller lifecycle cascade.

Notary equivocation evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id plus the two conflicting Seal wire objects: same (realm_id, notary_seq) slot with different canonical bytes, or a notary_seq=k+1 Seal that does not descend from the same signer's notary_seq=k Seal (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.1). Admission is verification-only: any Realm member MAY submit and the two conflicting notary signatures are the complete authorization; no capability grant is consulted and reducer MUST NOT require one. Reducer MUST re-verify both signatures and the slot rule, then add a per-signer fault record to the notary_fault cell. Once a fault record is accepted: receivers MUST reject later Seals signed by the fault signer, the two conflicting Seals and their descendants enter fork_quarantine, and Realm-wide pause applies only when no eligible signer remains.

Notary censorship evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id, the signed control-plane receipt, the seal_ref of the Seal that was obliged to include / signed-reject / defer the pending Control Move, a control_event_set_root non-membership proof for the censored event digest, and the missing rejection-or-defer proof (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.2). Admission is verification-only: the receipt holder MAY submit; the receipt signature plus the non-membership proof are the complete authorization. This evidence does NOT automatically disqualify the notary: reducer adds an audit fault record that MUST raise governance alarms, feeds inclusion-list / recovery obligations, and is evaluated by governance or the genesis recovery path.

Realm-scoped MemberIdentity segment replacement event. Append-only log entry that may supersede prior ak.member.identity.update events via payload.replaces[] without overloading ak.profile.update patch semantics.

Strand business-progression stage transition. Single source of truth for mutating Strand.stage / Strand.stage_changed_at; ak.strand.update patch on those paths MUST be rejected (forbidden-wire). The payload intentionally carries no reason / note / explanation field — rationale belongs in a Message on the Strand's discussion track that 'references' this event, and the event log's own actor_id / created_at is the audit source. Reducer enforces hard invariants from zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3: state=redacted yields failed_precondition reason=strand_already_terminal; state=archived yields strand_not_active; same-value self-transition is accepted but does NOT update stage_changed_at; reducer overwrites any wire-supplied stage_changed_at with the event's created_at. A per-Realm workflow profile MAY narrow which transitions are legal beyond these hard invariants.

Unified Strand tracks patch. payload.patch uses ak.patch.v1 against the Strand.tracks map: keys are track names (e.g. `synthesis`, `discussion`), values are patch ops that may toggle enabled, set is_primary, or modify profile / metadata on a track entry. Atomic across multiple tracks.

Strand move between Spaces (target_space_id in payload). Writes a cas_register cell keyed by (board_space_id, strand_id); the contains Relation list_space_id->strand_id is derived from cell value, not a separate truth source. Plane ruling (CBA): ak.component.strand.position.v1 defaults to sealed=true (control plane), so ak.strand.move is a Control Move carrying seal_basis; Realm schema MAY redeclare the cell family as data-plane mv_register + user-pick or per-object sequencer per authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 9.4 and models/realm-and-space.md section 3.6.

Strand reorder within Space. Writes the same cell as ak.strand.move; effect.list_space_id MUST equal head_eq.list_space_id (rank-only update). Plane ruling follows ak.strand.move: same cell family, same default sealed=true control-plane declaration (models/realm-and-space.md section 3.6).

Set or clear a per-(strand, actor) watch subscription. Writes a cas_register cell keyed by (strand_id, watcher_actor_id). Payload carries level in {mentions_only, participating, all, muted} (or null to clear, equivalent to mentions_only). Default invariant: payload.watcher_actor_id MUST equal envelope actor_id, unless writer holds ak.strand.watch.set.others. Cross-actor writes MUST carry refs[role=audit_pair] to a same-batch ak.audit.accessed event with access_kind=watch_set_others. The watches Relation (actor --watches--> strand) is a derived projection of this cell, not a separate truth source — direct ak.relation.create relation_kind=watches MUST schema_violation. See models/strand-and-message.md §8.
Space create (board / list / swimlane / calendar bucket / etc.)
Space metadata update (title, rank, kind-specific fields)

Space parent declaration. Parent is another ak:space: or null; cross-Realm parent is navigation only and never propagates Realm membership, capabilities, history, E2EE keys, retention, or federation policy.
Space archive (UI-level grouping archive; contained Strands MUST be relocated or follow archive)
Space restore (transition state archived -> active; only valid when current state == archived; tombstoned Spaces MUST NOT be restored)
Space tombstone (irreversible; contained Strands MUST be relocated before)

Controller-authored durable Sidecar exchange control. The outer payload exposes only private Strand routing plus an MLS encrypted payload whose plaintext validates as ak.schema.agent_sidecar_exchange_control.v1. It is accepted only in the matching Sidecar backing Circle from that Sidecar controller and is the sole truth source for coordinator reassignment and terminal exchange state.
Message-scoped redaction; does not grant generic redaction authority
Generic redaction envelope for non-message objects/events and profile-declared content trimming

Morph schema_refs[] migration. First-class event for evolving a Morph's schema_refs[] without bypassing audit / capability gates. Carries (from_schema_refs[], to_schema_refs[], compatibility_class, migration_evidence?). Required capability ak.morph.schema_migrate (high risk tier; see capability-action-registry.json). compatibility_class = additive | breaking | transformation; core reducers MUST reject breaking/transformation unless the Realm declares ak.profile.morph.schema_migration_transformations.v1. See zh/models/morph.md §4.1 S3.

Morph business-progression stage transition. Single source of truth for mutating Morph.stage / Morph.stage_changed_at; ak.morph.update / ak.morph.schema_migrate patches on those paths MUST be rejected (forbidden-wire). The payload intentionally carries no reason / note / explanation field — rationale belongs in a Message on an associated discussion track that 'references' this event. Reducer enforces hard invariants from zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3: state=redacted yields failed_precondition reason=morph_already_terminal; state=archived yields morph_not_active; same-value self-transition is accepted but does NOT update stage_changed_at; reducer overwrites any wire-supplied stage_changed_at with the event's created_at.

Agent signing key authorization. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_authorize_payload and bind agent_id, key_id, verification_method, accountable_principal_id, agent_key_scope, audience, issued_at, and approval_evidence; expires_at is optional (absent means non-expiring, revocation-governed). The agent-key cell is an observed-remove OR-Set. First authorization adds one authorization dot. Same-key re-authorization MUST atomically remove every active authorization dot visible at the Move seal_basis and add the replacement dot; it MUST NOT select a winner by arrival time. Concurrent replacement dots that survive the join are evaluated by the deterministic strictest fold: intersect agent_key_scope and audience, take the earliest finite expires_at (absence is +infinity), and fail closed if accountable_principal_id or verification_method disagree. Key replacement has no dedicated rotate kind: runtime replacement re-pairing authorizes the new key and revokes every prior active key (reason=superseded_by_repairing) in the same accepted transaction.

Agent signing key revocation. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_revoke_payload and bind agent_id, key_id, revoked_at, and revoked_by; the revocation's control-plane basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis, and its cutoff is the accepted Seal covering the Move.

Controller-owned signed selector statement binding (controller_subject, agent_slug) to one native personal agent DID. The Event belongs in the controller Principal Control Realm, never the Agent PCR or a Collaboration Realm. Concurrent distinct current values remain visible and make selector resolution ambiguous/fail-closed.

Agent lifecycle transition to paused state. Authorization basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis; payload carries no independent frontier. Auth Server MUST reject new agent session grants for this principal; existing tokens fail closed within an independent pause revocation freshness window of at most 60 seconds, never merely the session maximum TTL. Reversible via ak.self.agent.resume.

Agent lifecycle transition from paused to active. Authorization basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis; payload carries no independent frontier. At acceptance the reducer MUST use the accepted current control frontier to re-validate controller, agent, key, capability, Realm policy, and accountability_grant freshness; any failure rejects the resume.

Agent lifecycle terminal state. MUST fan-out ak.agent.key.revoke for all active agent keys, ak.capability.revoke for all unrevoked grants, and runtime endpoint revocation. Terminal — no transition out.

Agent-initiated draft proposal. Submitted by agent runtime; Principal Server materializes accepted drafts into controller-owned ak.agent.draft.v1 account-data after capability / policy / accountability / risk check. MUST NOT enter shared Realm history.
Agent-initiated action request. Carries proposed_action, target descriptor, and content digest. Awaits controller approval before generating shared event.

Controller approval of a draft / action request. Binds draft_id, content digest, target descriptor, proposed_action, approved payload digest, approval expiry, and single-use nonce. Publish executor MUST atomic-consume the nonce; reuse fails closed (reason=approval_already_consumed).
Controller rejection of a draft / action request. Draft transitions to rejected; agent runtime MUST NOT continue publish attempts.
Holder-private consent declaration: 'I consent to receive <consent_scope> from <peer>'
Revoke a previously granted consent (shares the ak.consent.grant cell; semantically a remove on the consent or_set)
Principal-scoped contact request fact. Issuer is requester; target holder must respond with accepted/rejected.
Principal-scoped contact acceptance fact. Issuer is original request target and MUST reference target-controlled consent grants.
Principal-scoped contact rejection fact. Issuer is original request target and does not write consent.
Principal-scoped contact tombstone fact. Issuer ends their own side of a contact and may revoke contact-managed consent dots.
Principal-scoped binding from unordered participant pair to canonical DM Realm and main Strand.
Realm-scoped profile override. payload.target_realm_id is the target Realm and no Space boundary is created.

B-model DID-root recovery re-anchor. Accepted only as the first event of an atomic re-anchor plus replacement-authorize unit in a principal control Realm. It fences the old device generation against the complete accepted Seal frontier and preserves every same-version candidate for deterministic conflict quarantine.
Key backup active series selection for one principal and backup_class.

Push route binding for a (recipient_service_id, principal, device, push_route) tuple. Carries push_target_id, push_gateway_did, encryption_key, capabilities. Stored as actor-private state on the recipient Principal Server only; MUST NOT be replicated to Principal Servers outside the binding's recipient_service_id context.
MLS commit or Welcome processing failure diagnostic
Realm history key request (receiver to key source); ephemeral to-device signal relayed to the target source, not a reducer-input durable event
Realm key share: member-device history key delivery or RRK durability seal

Auditable access marker for privileged reads or privacy-sensitive paired writes. E2EE compliance release uses ak.audit.release; ak.audit.accessed remains for non-release audit pairs such as Circle metadata audit, watch_set_others, late recovery, and policy reads.

Audit Applet Binding. Declares that an audit applet/service may request staged historical release sessions for a specific Realm or Circle effective_scope. Binding is control-plane only: it does not add the applet to MLS, does not subscribe it to realtime sync, and does not grant plaintext/history keys. Bindings are non-retroactive: activation_frontier_digest / first_auditable_epoch define the earliest eligible material, and later policy changes MUST NOT expand eligibility for already encrypted messages.
Audit release session request. Must reference an active ak.audit.applet_binding and a bounded historical target range or target_refs.
Audit release session authorization by a scoped approver. Approves only the intersection of request, binding, policy, and effective_scope.
Member-visible notice for an audit release session. Circle-scoped notices are visible only to the target Circle audience and authorized moderators/admins.

Sealed audit release manifest. Appends to the session release log only while the session FSM head is notice. Records exactly which historical target_refs or sealed epochs were released, to whom, under which binding/session/notice/policy. Current active epoch release is forbidden; sealed epoch releases must reference sealed_by_commit_ref. Same-basis close dominates release and rejects the release.

Close an audit release session and freeze its final release_refs. release_refs MUST exactly equal the accepted ordered release log at the close seal_basis. Close is terminal; for same-basis close versus release, close wins and the competing release is rejected.
Signed hard-erasure receipt. Attests deletion outcome and retained verification stub within an issuer-declared storage boundary; does not prove independent third-party copies disappeared.

Range-bound completeness attestation. Distinct from ak.audit.ryw_receipt (per-event read-your-writes hint) and ak.event_batch_receipt (set-bound integrity hint): this attestation asserts completeness over an explicit (from_frontier, to_frontier) + per-actor seq interval range. Issuer commits to having observed every reducer-input event in scope; witness quorum or independent seal backing is required for non-self-attested deployments. See zh/sync/operations-sync.md §6.4.
Lift a previously sealed moderation decision (observed-remove/supersede the referenced decision in ak.component.moderation_state.v1)

Submit an appeal against an existing ak.moderation.decision. Writes the appeal cell to state=submitted. Schema: ak.schema.moderation_appeal.v1. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5 (appeal strand).
Reviewer acknowledges the appeal and transitions cell state submitted → under_review. Identifies the reviewing actor and target appeal. Schema: ak.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Reviewer's verdict on the appeal: uphold (decision stands) / overturn (decision reversed, emits ak.moderation.decision.lift) / modify (decision adjusted). Transitions cell state under_review → decided. Schema: ak.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Closes the appeal from submitted / under_review / decided via reviewer close, appellant withdrawal, or a deployment's authorized close service. close is a manual/authorized action; the protocol does not mandate any auto-close timer or cool-off duration (deployment/Realm policy decides). Schema: ak.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Read cursor advance event (actor-private). Writes the actor's latest read position for a given (realm_id, read_scope) tuple. Was historically named ak.read.cursor; renamed to align the event_kind, capability action, schema id and typed ID prefix on a single noun root read_cursor.

Invite create. Directed v1 invite payloads carry invitee plus invite_delivery_target and introduction_evidence_digest; raw locator tokens and invite_receive_policy state are private and MUST NOT enter the durable Realm event.

reducer_effects: match pending ak.invite.third_party by invite_id and token_commitment
re-check verification_service_id against current effective Realm allowlist
deduplicate (invite_id, claim_nonce) and token_commitment before accepting
transition invite cell pending -> claimed and materialize subject-bound membership proposal
expire and clean pending invite material before claim acceptance when expires_at <= now

registry_rules: A schema row with omitted status defaults to active. New or edited rows MUST spell status explicitly.
Allowed status values are active and deprecated. Deprecated rows remain resolvable for historical data but MUST NOT be produced by new writes.

The effective schema reference of a row is the literal concatenation (file + optional fragment): fragment already includes its leading '#', so consumers MUST NOT insert another separator. For example file='schemas/agent-operations.schema.json' plus fragment='#/$defs/agent_pairing_bootstrap' resolves to exactly 'schemas/agent-operations.schema.json#/$defs/agent_pairing_bootstrap'. Consumers MUST resolve that URI-fragment JSON Pointer and MUST NOT bind schema_id to the top-level document of file. When fragment is absent, the effective reference is the top-level document of file. Two schema_id rows mapping to the same file MUST be distinguished by fragment (or one MUST omit fragment to denote the whole document); a consumer that ignores fragment and loads the top-level document for a fragment-bearing row is non-conforming.

fragment, when present, MUST be a non-empty RFC 6901 JSON Pointer in URI-fragment representation starting with '#/'. If the pointer does not resolve within file, or a row that shares a file with another row omits fragment while that other row also omits fragment (ambiguous whole-document mapping), consumers MUST fail closed rather than silently pick a schema.

schemas.description: Shared coarse JSON Schema shapes for Arkret human identifiers, IDNA domains, handles, acct URIs, and human-readable text profiles.
Issuer-signed accountability endorsement for Actor Profile accountable_principal_ids verification.
Signed controller-scoped native personal agent selector claim for @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug> resolution.
Controller-signed, verifier-bound private disclosure of a managed Agent's immutable requested_scope; the public Agent DID carries only its commitment digest.
Controller-signed minimal public binding from a Native Agent verification method to raw Ed25519 key material and one accepted Agent key authorization.
Portable Native Agent signer authorization, state-witness, and freshness evidence used outside the ordinary device directory.
Authenticated shared-context Agent signer evidence query request.
Closed outcome carrying portable Agent signer evidence or non-enumerating per-selector failures.

storage_rules: Protocol wire objects, canonical JSON, signatures, hashes, fixtures, logs, API DTOs, and cross-service references MUST use the full typed form ak:<kind>:<uuid> unless a special form below applies.

Storage implementations MAY store raw 16-byte UUID values (e.g. PostgreSQL `uuid` column) without the ak:<kind>: prefix when the table, column, or explicit kind field already supplies the type context.
Implementations that store raw IDs MUST restore the full typed form before computing canonical JSON, event IDs, payload hashes, detached proofs, federation payloads, sync cursors, or audit logs.
The <kind> segment is part of the signed/canonical wire value. It MUST NOT be changed, inferred differently, or stripped during verification, forwarding, backfill, or replay.

The UUID segment MUST be RFC 9562 UUID version 7 (48-bit Unix-millisecond timestamp + 4-bit version=7 + 12-bit rand_a + 2-bit variant=10b + 62-bit rand_b), serialized as the canonical 36-character lowercase hex form `xxxxxxxx-xxxx-7xxx-Nxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx` where N ∈ {8,9,a,b}.

registry_rules: New operation_id values MUST be added here before any OpenAPI, HTTP binding table, SDK generator, or alternative transport binding references them.
Generated views MAY change shape, grouping, or field order, but MUST NOT introduce, rename, or remove operation_id values that are absent from this catalog.
Supporting Arkret core does not imply support for every registered operation. Implementations MUST advertise supported_operations and supported_profiles explicitly.

Each surface_groups entry carries a tier (see capability_tiers); only the core tier is implied by claiming v1 protocol support. Extension, interop_bridge, and deployment_local surfaces require explicit advertisement.

Profile matrices in artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json define role-level MUST/SHOULD requirements; the surface groups below define machine-readable capability families for discovery, docs, and lint.
Each operation MUST declare success_shape_kind so SDKs can determine success handling without endpoint-name hard-coding.

Operations with typed OpenAPI bodies SHOULD declare request_schema_ref and/or response_schema_ref. The referenced schema fragment is the source for generated DTO docs and MUST match the OpenAPI component referenced by the HTTP binding.

Operations that still bind OpenAPI request/response bodies to OperationRequest or OperationResult MUST declare generic_binding with request/response booleans, reason, profile_gate, and migration_plan; core-tier operations MUST NOT use generic bindings.

operation_id values MUST end with <kind>.<action>. The kind segment MUST be one of query, stream, resource, command, upload, or exchange; the action segment MUST describe protocol semantics and MUST NOT be an HTTP method name.

resource.replace operations MUST bind to HTTP PUT; resource.delete operations MUST bind to HTTP DELETE; command, upload, exchange, and complex query body operations SHOULD bind to HTTP POST unless their operation notes define a stricter resource URI replacement contract.

Every write operation (kind command/upload/exchange, and resource.replace / resource.delete) MUST declare idempotency_mechanism (one of idempotency_key, object_id, request_id, canonical_hash, protocol_sequence, none) and retry_safe (boolean). Read-only operations (query/stream/resource.get/resource.head) MUST NOT declare these fields.

idempotency_mechanism is the machine-readable source of truth for which idempotency mechanism from api-conventions.md section 6 an operation uses. canonical_hash operations MUST also declare canonical_hash_input as either full_body or an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer. retry_safe=true means a byte-identical full retry of the same request cannot produce duplicate side effects: it returns the original outcome, an equivalent idempotent no-op, or a deterministic conflict. retry_safe=false means blind retries MAY duplicate side effects or consume one-time material; clients MUST NOT retry such operations without out-of-band reconciliation.

capability_tiers.core: Base interoperable surfaces implied by claiming Arkret v1 protocol support (service discovery, identity registry, events/account aggregate).
capability_tiers.extension: Optional interoperable surfaces that are part of the Arkret specification but require explicit discovery/profile advertisement.
capability_tiers.interop_bridge: Adapter surfaces that bridge Arkret to external protocols (MIMI Internet-Drafts, third-party Applet hosts). Implementations advertise these only when the external protocol is supported; bridge operations are not part of any core or extension profile and frequently mirror an in-spec operation via bridges_to.
capability_tiers.deployment_local: Deployment-specific, operator, or product-local surfaces that MUST NOT be assumed from core protocol support alone.

operations.notes: Account Authority exchanges an OIDC authorization code for an opaque, short-lived account_handoff_grant bound to the request DPoP key. The handoff is not ak.session.grant, has no refresh-token semantics, and its closed operation allowlist is issue_identity_binding_challenge, register, and issue_session_grant. It returns bound, identity_creation_active, or identity_creation_busy state and atomically acquires, renews, or fences an identity-creation lease for the authenticated service account. Repeating the same request_id returns the same live outcome. A different holder cannot take an unexpired lease; after expiry, a newly authenticated holder for the same service account may fence it and must preserve any reserved principal_id, operation digest, and public DID-operation checkpoint.

Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header. The Account Authority verifies the current lease holder and fence, validates the complete unpublished DID operation, derives principal_id and its canonical operation digest, persists the public operation checkpoint, renews the same-holder lease, and issues a <=300s single-use challenge bound to account, holder cnf.jkt, lease/fence, principal_id, operation digest, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose, and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory.

Canonical account creation/binding operation. In the account-first identity_creation branch the caller MUST present Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus matching DPoP, the current lease/fence, the exact reserved DID inception operation, and a fresh identity-root control proof over the persisted challenge transcript. For did:webvh inception the verifier takes parameters.updateKeys[0] from the operation itself (the root is not a DID Document verificationMethod) and requires verification_key_multibase to match it exactly. The Account Authority CAS-validates account/holder/lease/fence/reservation, consumes the challenge, submits the DID operation internally, accepts only accepted or byte-identical duplicate with a verified head digest, and writes the service-account binding. The (account, principal_id, operation_digest) result is idempotent; published-but-not-yet-bound state is durably completed for that same account and can never be rebound to another account. The operation never accepts recovery words, seed material, or identity-root private keys.

Authorizes a sibling device after the verified current device confirms the SAS/QR transcript. When device_pairing_request_id is present, the Account Authority MUST atomically require and consume the unexpired pending staged record whose pairing_code, new_device_pubkey and challenge_signature exactly match the request; a mismatch performs no device authorization.

Managed-DID (account-authority) device enrollment, device-lifecycle.md §5.4 / key-management.md §5.0.6. The authenticated session asks its designated enrollment authority to mint a service_attested ak.device.authorize for this session's own device; the authority signs with its persistent enrollment key (never the principal SSK) and returns the full Event. The caller submits it verbatim to POST /_arkret/self/events. Distinct from pair_device (§2.1), which lands an existing-device SAS/QR approval and carries a pairing_code; enroll_device is only the bootstrap / first-device path where no sibling device can approve. The authority MUST require actor_seq=1, a verified identity-creation binding receipt for the same principal/account, and no existing active device; a bare session grant or actor_seq>1 MUST NOT enroll a second long-term device. Later devices use pair_device or the recovery re-anchor strand.

Account Authority single-call session-grant exchange. The response is the client-visible SessionGrantOutcome; any Principal-side local session provisioning is internal. There is no separate client-visible grant-to-bearer exchange step: the client presents ak.session.grant directly to /_arkret/self/* with DPoP (api-conventions §3.3). For proof_kind=oidc_code_exchange, the Account Authority exchanges the authorization code and validates issuer/state/nonce/redirect_uri/principal/device/audience binding. For proof_kind=pre_registration_handoff, the caller instead presents Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus matching DPoP; the handoff's service account MUST already be bound to the requested principal_id. principal_id is required for every proof kind and MUST already have a verified account binding; unknown or unbound returns principal_unknown (404). The Account Authority MUST NOT derive or mint a principal DID from OIDC. A first OIDC interaction may create only the account handoff; the client completes cold-root custody and canonical register before requesting a session grant. For proof_kind=agent_key_proof when high-risk scope needs controller approval, the endpoint returns 403 ErrorEnvelope with error.code=claim_required and closed agent_human_approval_error_details; it never returns CAPTCHA, OTP, password, or browser challenge material to the runtime.

DPoP-bound session-grant rotation (account-lifecycle §4.1, device-lifecycle §3.3). An authorized device presents a DPoP holder proof for the grant's cnf.jkt plus a fresh DID/device proof bound to principal_id, device_id, audience, request_canonical_digest, challenge, issued_at, and expires_at; expires_at - issued_at MUST be <=300s. The old grant is single-use revoked. Account Authority-local op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority to Auth Server S2S Auth-side logout sub-operation (account-lifecycle §4.1): the Account Authority has already validated the client-visible ak.gate.account.command.logout request, then calls this operation with service-to-service authentication to log out the Auth-side browser/auth session owning the presented ak.session.grant and terminate that session's grant rotation chain. Ordinary clients MUST NOT call this operation; they only call ak.gate.account.command.logout. HTTP-only S2S op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Server-to-server session-grant introspection (RFC 7662-style). The Principal Server validating a presented grant calls this with the grant id or grant_jwt (+ optional audience and optional S2S holder confirmation) and learns whether it is active, plus non-secret grant metadata. The introspection response MUST include the grant's cnf_jkt (RFC 7638 thumbprint of the bound DPoP holder key) so the Principal Server can verify the per-request DPoP proof on /_arkret/self/* (api-conventions §3.3); clients do not send a separate introspection-proof header on self-path requests. session_public_key is also returned for RFC 9421 PoP verification. READ-ONLY: introspection MUST NOT consume/revoke the grant. Authenticated by the configured session_grant_introspection_bearer (server-local); not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority ordinary hard logout (account-lifecycle §4.1): single client-visible logout entry. The handler validates the current ak.session.grant + DPoP, terminates the Auth-side auth session / grant rotation chain through ak.gate.account.command.logout_auth_session when Auth-side is split out, and completes or durably schedules the Principal-side local account session + device session cleanup and to-device/push removal. Distinct from revoke_session (targeted session-grant revoke). HTTP-only Account Authority op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Unauthorized, nonexistent, and foreign-controller IDs use one indistinguishable not_found envelope. The backing Circle is included only as the Sidecar object's reducer-managed security binding and never as an ordinary Circle resource.

Enqueues caller-supplied DeviceMessageEnvelope targets into recipient device queues. Each target carries a sender-assigned message_id copied unchanged into the stored envelope; the service deduplicates logical messages by (sender_principal_id, sender_device_id, message_id), returning the existing outcome for identical canonical target content and duplicate_conflict/message_id_conflict for different content. HTTP batch replay is additionally deduplicated by (sender, Idempotency-Key). Queue pruning is only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.

Explicit, cumulative, monotonic to-device delivery acknowledgement (client-sync.md §10.1). Queue deletion happens only here; stream cursor advancement (account subscribe after=, device_messages after=) is read-only and MUST NOT prune the queue. Re-acking the same or an older token is a legal no-op. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens are rejected with invalid_param (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything.
Writes requester-side ak.contact.requested fact and requester-side consent grants for requested scopes; MUST NOT write target consent or accepted fact.
Target-side accept/reject of a contact request. Accept writes target-controlled consent grants; reject writes no consent.
Holder contact projection from contact facts plus consent-derived directional scopes; account-data contact notes are local decoration only.
Holder-side contact tombstone. Default revocation is limited to contact-managed active consent dots.

Read the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. Returns the recommended default when no explicit override is stored; the response is never written into the target Realm durable event log.

Replace the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. The body MUST set subject_id equal to the session actor; the override shares the same store as ak.self.contact.command.tombstone(block_peer) blocked_subjects writes.
Issues a fresh opaque locator for the authenticated principal. subject_id and recipient_service_id are server-derived; the raw bearer token is returned exactly once and MUST NOT be persisted.

Atomically revokes one authenticated-principal-owned locator and issues a new opaque token. The old token becomes indistinguishable from unknown tokens before success is returned. After an uncertain transport outcome, the client MUST first idempotently revoke the old locator_id and only then issue fresh material; directly issuing without that revocation can leave the old token active.
Idempotently revokes one locator owned by the authenticated principal. A same-principal retry returns the original revoked_at. Unknown, consumed, or cross-principal locator ids return not_found.

Idempotent resolver for accepted contacts. Requires accepted contact projection and direct_message consent. Cross-Principal-Server create=true uses two participant-authoring stages: a reserved remote KeyPackage claim draft is signed and resubmitted before the binding Event draft; only found is an active success state.

Builds a ak.circle.create Operation in the named parent Realm and routes it through the local accept pipeline. Reducer-locked fields (mls_group_ref, state) MUST NOT be actor-supplied; encryption_profile='none' is allowed only when the parent Realm policy floor permits plaintext.
Lists Circles the caller may see within one parent Realm (required realm_id query). Directory visibility is enforced per Circle; non-members of a 'members'-visibility Circle MUST NOT see it.
Reads one Circle projection. Returns not_found when the Circle is invisible to the caller rather than disclosing existence.

Builds ak.circle.member.state. Activating another actor requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to this Circle, and the target MUST already be a joined parent-Realm member (strict-subset invariant); a self-join is gated by join_rule.
Builds ak.circle.member.state with membership=leave for the path actor_id.

Rotates the Circle's bound MLS group. MUST NOT acknowledge a rotation without actually changing the cryptographic scope; returns unsupported_feature until the MLS genesis/commit/welcome cascade is wired end-to-end.
Builds ak.circle.archive; transition follows the Circle lifecycle matrix (reducer rejects illegal transitions with circle_not_active).

Builds ak.circle.restore; transition follows the Circle lifecycle matrix (reducer rejects illegal transitions with circle_not_archived). Restore re-enables new writes after pending MLS membership removals are settled.
Builds ak.circle.tombstone (terminal). Response surfaces the terminal state with empty members.

Resource-side appeal against an operator takedown. The appeal packet MUST bind takedown_id, resource id, appellant DID, argument/evidence digest, requested_outcome and created_at, signed by the resource governance key or an authorized advocate; the Directory returns a signed decision receipt. See discovery-directory.md §8.7.

Return one bounded, manifest-committed chunk of a complete_control_state_v1 proof bundle for one authenticated, caller-visible Realm/scope. The request MUST name an exact locally trusted_anchor_seal_id and chunk_index; later chunks pin expected_bundle_digest. The service MUST build from that anchor and return mls_governance_anchor_unreachable instead of substituting another anchor. The service derives membership_frontier and all governance roots from one accepted Seal view; callers cannot supply roots. Responses bind canonical acquisition identity with proof_request_digest, commit all chunks under chunks_root, and use bundle_digest rather than accepted_seal_id as the logical content address. Each response is at most 4 MiB; the logical bundle is at most 256 MiB, 1024 chunks, 4096 Seals, 1048576 covered digests, 262144 control leaves and 128 frontier Events. Exceeding a total bound returns mls_governance_proof_bounds_exceeded with no partial output. Implementations MUST enforce Realm/scope visibility before materialization and MUST fail closed when any covered Event, control state, Seal path, chunk commitment, signature authority, or reducer profile cannot be reconstructed.

HTTP-specific POST/body form of ak.events.query. Semantically identical (same selector / cursor / order / filter / include_completeness parameter set, same response shape including optional range_completeness). Choose when URL length would exceed practical limits (large realms[]/actors[] arrays, complex filters object) or when query parameters would be logged inadvertently by proxies. Non-HTTP transports MUST use the canonical ak.self.events.query.scan binding (SelfEvents/Query / self.events.query.scan), not expose this variant as a separate gRPC or MQ operation.
Dereference a known set of event_id / event_digest references to full EventEnvelope objects. Point lookup by identifier, not a range scan — use ak.self.events.query.scan for selector-based reads.

Long-lived per-Realm / actor event stream with optional bounded catch-up replay. `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same caller/selector scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After.

Durable self event submission, including ak.invite.claim. For ak.invite.claim, the receiving Realm reducer is the authoritative state machine: it MUST match token_commitment, re-check verification_service_id allowlist against current Realm policy, reject claim_nonce replay, perform pending -> claimed / membership-proposal effects, and run expiry cleanup before accepting.

Submit a client-signed Seal. Except for the canonical genesis exception, the signature MUST satisfy the predecessor governance state's ak.component.notary.v1 membership and threshold rules; Realm visibility or device ownership is insufficient. The receiver recomputes the Seal id, recursive coverage, completeness_root, state_root, signer authority and signature.
Federation peer Events surface describe. This endpoint describes the server-to-server peer event bindings; it is not a client self/events binding.

Federation peer frontier probe. Requires service-to-service authentication, Source/Destination service DID headers, trust-domain headers, and Realm federation_peer authorization. It returns the federation peer frontier response shape on the dedicated peer trust surface.

Federation peer pull/backfill query. Uses the same selector, cursor, order, and response semantics as ak.self.events.query.scan, but the HTTP trust surface is peer and the caller MUST be an authorized federation peer service.

HTTP-specific POST/body form of ak.peer.events.query.scan. Semantically identical to GET /_arkret/peer/events; use it when federation selectors or filters are too large or sensitive for query strings.

Federation peer event reference resolution for missing prev_refs / causal references. Requires authorized federation peer service authentication and applies the same reference-disclosure and history-visibility rules as peer event query.

Federation peer event push. Body is EventsSubmitFederationRequestBody and the caller MUST use service-to-service authentication with Source/Destination service DID and trust-domain headers. Federated ak.invite.claim events are still decided by the destination Realm reducer, which MUST enforce token_commitment, current allowlist re-check, claim_nonce replay rejection, membership proposal conversion, and expiry cleanup; peer ingress prechecks are not state authority.

Private Principal Server to Principal Server invite delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-ID equal to invite_address.recipient_service_id, a ak.invite.create event whose invitee equals invite_address.subject_id, and introduction_evidence accepted by the recipient invite_receive_policy.

Private Principal Server to Principal Server contact and Direct Conversation binding fact delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-ID equal to contact_address.recipient_service_id, and an original signed ak.contact.* or ak.direct_conversation.bound envelope that the recipient projects without re-signing.

Atomic cross-Principal-Server KeyPackage claim. The destination KeyPackage authority is the sole CAS authority and MUST validate both the requester participant authorization and the outer source-service HTTP Message Signature. Idempotency is scoped by (Source-Service-ID, claim_request_id) and binds the canonical request digest; duplicate transport delivery returns the original outcome, but callers MUST use the query operation rather than replaying the command after an uncertain outcome. Success omits inventory counts and per-device failures.

Read-only recovery of the destination authority's durable peer-claim ledger after an uncertain command outcome. It requires the same authenticated source service and exact request_digest and returns only opaque claim state plus the original signed success outcome when one exists.
Federation peer snapshot manifest head for snapshot-assisted bootstrap. Requires service-to-service authentication and Realm federation_peer authorization.

Canonical broadcast ephemeral send operation for ak.schema.ephemeral_envelope.v1. Carries ak.presence, ak.typing, ak.receipt.read, and ak.call.signal; MUST NOT persist the signal as a durable Event or advance actor_seq / Realm frontier.

Media service token exchange operation. Issues a short-lived (TTL <= 600s) backend_token + participant_binding for joining a focus declared in ak.realm.media_service.foci[]. Same wire across all backend types (livekit / mediasoup / janus / arkret-native); only backend_token shape is type-specific. Token issuer DID MUST be one of the Realm-authorized media service DIDs; clients reject otherwise (token_issuer_unauthorised). See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3.

The wrapper carries one complete DID method-native operation. did_method is the bare method discriminator and MUST equal the DID method component. Controller/update/recovery authorization comes only from the native operation; transport authentication is admission-only. Unsupported methods, generic replace/patch/document fallbacks, stale heads, and sibling forks fail closed. Exact canonical-operation retries are duplicate-success without a second history append.

Idempotently return or create the service DID bound to the canonical (service_type, public_base) registration key. The client supplies and controls a signed did:webvh inception operation; the Provider verifies the proof and endpoint binding and never receives private key material. Provider persistence MUST enforce UNIQUE(service_type, public_base) and MUST reject an existing hosted document that declares the same key even when the mapping row is absent.
Read the service registration bound to the canonical (service_type, public_base) key without creating or mutating identity state.

Read the currently accepted ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 projection for the authenticated or explicitly selected principal. Returns active_policy=null when no accepted policy exists; does not publish, rotate, or revoke policy state.

Publish a signed ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 genesis policy or rotation for the authenticated principal. HTTP binding is POST because the principal/authority is derived from authenticated proof and signed policy state rather than a URI-addressed resource slot. Servers MUST verify auth_data.signed_fields, signature authority, version monotonicity, and supersedes linkage before accepting.

Resolves a short-lived agent pairing token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The pairing token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is the six-field agent_pairing_bootstrap.

Runtime-to-controller pending approval request for native personal-agent key pairing. The runtime proves possession of the local key and the short pairing code; the controller still must approve by signing ak.agent.key.authorize. The pairing code and proof-of-possession MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string. One open pairing_request_id has at most one pending stable ak.agent.runtime_key_binding.v1 digest: same-binding retries retain approval/notification ids and update freshness proof, while a different binding fails with HTTP 409 agent_runtime_request_conflict without replacement.

Runtime-side poll for the controller decision on a previously submitted runtime key request. The pairing_request_id + pairing_code + agent_id triple is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; a record miss and a pairing_code or agent_id mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). Once approved, the outcome carries authorized_event_ref plus the authorized key binding; the runtime MUST compare authorized_public_key_digest against its own key and treat a mismatch as paired-by-another-runtime. HTTP responses MUST carry Retry-After; clients wait at least that interval and use 1s/2s/5s/10s then at most 30s backoff, stopping after pairing expiry.

Unauthenticated stage of a device-pairing short-link handoff (device-lifecycle.md §2.1.1). The new device submits new_device_pubkey and challenge_signature (plus optional display_name / device_metadata); the service mints a fresh device_pairing_request_id and an 8-character Crockford-style 40-bit CSPRNG pairing_code and stores a bounded-TTL account-less record in state pending_authorization. The staged record binds no principal and grants nothing until an authenticated device authorizes it. Stage, resolve and status are rate limited. Each call mints a fresh request, so blind retries duplicate staged records: not retry-safe.

Resolves a device-pairing short-link token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The pairing token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is the DevicePairingBootstrap. resolve MUST return a uniform not_found for unknown id, pairing_code mismatch, expiry, or a non-pending record so the failing condition is not enumerable. Authorization is unchanged: the returned bootstrap is only consumed by an authenticated device driving ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.

Unauthenticated poll for the authorization status of a staged device-pairing record. The device_pairing_request_id + pairing_code pair is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; a record miss and a pairing_code mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). While the record is open the outcome carries only state pending_authorization; once an authenticated device has authorized the pairing the outcome carries state authorized plus required device_id and authorized_event_ref; an expired record reports only state expired during a bounded cleanup retention period and becomes not_found after deletion.

Resolves an online invite locator token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The locator token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is a signed principal_locator.
Canonical HTTP binding is POST /_arkret/self/policy/check. Paths carry no version segment; protocol version is negotiated via *.describe / supported_operations (see sync/api-conventions.md).
Lists typed cross-Realm links projected from ak.realm.link. direction is outbound/inbound/both; link_kind_allow is a comma-separated allowlist of canonical link kinds.

Builds an ak.realm.link Control Move from realm_id -> target_realm_id. General directed cycles are valid and traversal uses a visited set; admission rejects only self-reference, invalid kind, invalid payload, or an illegal FSM transition. Self-reference returns schema_violation with reason_code realm_link_self_reference; an illegal transition returns failed_precondition with reason_code realm_link_invalid_transition.

Writes a tombstoning ak.realm.link Move (status=tombstoned) for the (realm_id, target_realm_id, link_kind) triple. link_kind defaults to governed_by; callers may override via the link_kind query param.

Returns the merged effective policy after walking governed_by / inherits_policy_from ancestors per the Realm's ak.realm.inheritance_policy. inheritance_mode=none when no inheritance policy is projected (implicit inheritance is forbidden).

Returns the projected ak.realm.organization relationship statements for the Realm (active / revoked / expired, latest-per-(organization_id, relationship)) plus declared owning_organizations hints with no verified statement. The caller must be authorized to read the Realm. A relationship is only verified when lifecycle_phase=verified_active; declared_organization_hints are unverified claims and MUST NOT be rendered as official / governed / endorsed.
Reads the projected ak.realm.policy_server config. Returns not_found when neither the Realm nor its governed_by ancestor chain declared one. from_org_fallback=true marks an inherited config.

Builds a ak.realm.policy_server Move (admission capability ak.policy.manage). Reducer validates URL scheme and on_timeout enum. This admin DTO is a simplified projection of the canonical payload (server_id/endpoint/public_keys/applies_to/fail_mode).
Tombstones the per-Realm ak.realm.policy_server cell so callers fall back to the governed_by chain or local-only capability check. Empty success response.
Reads the Realm lifecycle projection (owner + members + deleted). Returns not_found when the Realm is invisible to the caller.

Builds a ak.realm.archive Move. The archived facet changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; archived=false clears the archived facet unless a terminal lifecycle state already applies.

Builds a ak.realm.freeze Move. The frozen facet changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; frozen=true rejects ordinary non-exempt writes with realm_frozen and frozen=false clears the freeze facet unless a terminal lifecycle state already applies.

Builds a terminal ak.realm.tombstone Move with a successor_realm_id. The tombstoned state changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; later ordinary writes fail with realm_terminal_state.
Builds a terminal ak.realm.destroy Move. The destroyed state changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; later ordinary writes fail with realm_terminal_state.
Full event-log + operation dump for a Realm (schema ak.export.realm.v1). Caller must be authorized to read the Realm; payload visibility still follows Realm policy.
Returns the organization-inherited effective moderation policy view: inheritance chain, organization policy layers, the Realm's own override, and merged effective rules.

Writes a Realm moderation-policy override (ak.realm.moderation_policy). Only the Realm owner may write; an override that loosens an action an organization policy denies requires explicit organization approval embedded in the document, otherwise the server returns failed_precondition with reason_code=requires_organization_approval.

Candidate-profile private application intake. The applicant-signed receipt binds the accepted knock, policy/revision/private-body digests and applicant DID. The receipt and private body commit atomically and never enter shared Realm history.

Candidate-profile private reviewer decision. The reviewer-signed receipt binds the exact application revision and a capability grant/frontier proof; stale, expired or unauthorized decisions fail closed.
Candidate-profile private applicant cancellation. The caller and detached receipt signer must both be the original applicant.
Lists candidate application metadata. Reviewers and each matching applicant receive the protected body; other Realm members receive only application_pending placeholders.
Reads one candidate application for its applicant or an eligible reviewer. Every successful private-body read emits ak.audit.accessed.
Reads only the profile-private submit/read/review/cancel/invite-consume audit trail for one application. Applicant, eligible reviewer, or explicitly authorized Realm auditor only.
Lists holder-private consent cells for the authenticated holder only. Peer actors MUST NOT receive cell state, dots, expiry or request timestamps.
Reads one holder-private consent cell. The authenticated actor MUST equal holder_did or be an explicitly authorised holder controller; peers never receive this DTO.
Builds a ak.consent.grant Control Move on the holder's consent cell. The authenticated actor MUST be authorized to write the holder's consent (holder or an explicitly authorized controller/agent).

Builds a ak.consent.revoke Control Move enumerating the active grant dots for the (consent_id, peer, consent_scope). Revoking consent_scope=any cascades all concrete scopes; revoking a concrete scope leaves others intact.

Submits an opaque consent-contact request from the authenticated peer. peer_did defaults to and MUST equal the actor. The response is identical for missing holders, policy denial, rate limiting, silent drop and quarantine acceptance; the operation never returns a consent cell.
Lists the authenticated actor's account_data entries. content is stored verbatim and is opaque to the server.
Reads one account_data entry by data_type key. Returns not_found when the key is unset.

Builds a ak.account_data.set actor-private write. Controller-private registered types reject agent / applet / service principals. content is stored verbatim; clients own canonical encoding and (for sensitive keys) client-side encryption.
Deletes one account_data entry and fans out an actor-private update to the holder's other devices.

Builds a ak.read_cursor.advance actor-private write for (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope, position). Multi-device convergence is by HLC max with device_id tiebreak; the cursor is never published into shared Realm history.
Lists the authenticated actor's read markers, optionally filtered by the realm_id query param.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Strand lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Morph lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Space lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface that materializes a View{kind=collection} projection such as board/list/table/calendar. The response is a derived read model computed from signed Events, reducer profile, View definition, and the returned frontier; it is not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface returning the authorized document body, version, relation, comment, and cursor-presence read-model for a single document Morph addressed within its Realm. Canonical truth remains the Morph/Relation/Message event history.

Holder-bound one-shot read of the current principal account projection. Returns principal_id, account lifecycle state, device summaries, optional ActorProfile, and signed handle-claim evidence or refs. It MUST NOT return an unsigned bare handle as authoritative identity. Naming: the trailing segment 'viewer' is intentionally outside the api-conventions.md §2.4 read-verb taxonomy; it follows the GraphQL 'viewer' convention (the authenticated subject's own projection). The target is located by the holder-bound session rather than an external id, so 'get' does not apply, and 'viewer' (subject identity projection) stays distinct from 'describe' (service capability metadata).

Holder-bound service wrapper around ak.profile.update / Actor Profile projection. Request body is a closed patch over display_name, avatar_blob_ref, and profile_fields.<key>; profile_fields.bio is the canonical personal bio field and avatar_url is not accepted on the Arkret protocol path.

Streaming push of cross-Realm account-aggregate deltas (cross-Realm frontier, to_device queue, account_data, device_lists, presence, unread / notification counts). Connection is long-lived; server pushes NDJSON frames as new data becomes available. Symmetric with ak.self.events.stream.subscribe — both are streaming subscriptions, differing only in scope (self.events.stream.subscribe = per-Realm event log; self.account.stream.subscribe = account-aggregate). `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same principal/device/filter scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After. Presence changes are sent through ak.self.ephemeral.command.send, not this read-only stream subscription.

High-assurance optional endpoint to revoke a previously issued cursor authority. Revocation hits return cursor_revoked and MUST NOT advance account subscribe position, barrier wait, or dropped recovery state. To-device queue deletion is decoupled from cursors entirely and happens only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.

success_shape_kind_definitions.service_describe: ServiceDescribe object returned by a describe endpoint.
success_shape_kind_definitions.schema_resource: Response body is a canonical artifact JSON Schema resource.
success_shape_kind_definitions.inline_response: Endpoint-specific inline object schema in OpenAPI.
success_shape_kind_definitions.operation_result: Generic OperationResult envelope; operation row MUST carry generic_binding.
success_shape_kind_definitions.event_stream: Long-lived event stream rather than a single JSON success body.
success_shape_kind_definitions.metadata_headers: Metadata-only success expressed through HTTP headers.

risk_tier_definitions.low: Read, projection, discovery, ack, and account-private affordances. Freshness fail-closed treats unknown / stale as local-pending allowed (capabilities.md §18).
risk_tier_definitions.medium: Object create / update / delete, message authoring, invite issuance, MLS proposal, audit query. Freshness requires recent frontier within freshness_required_ms.
risk_tier_definitions.high: Capability mutation, policy mutation, lifecycle freeze / tombstone / destroy, schema redefinition, MLS commit / welcome / genesis, audit export, moderation decision, admin / hierarchy / upgrade. Freshness MUST be within freshness_required_ms; partition forces local pending with no peer visibility.

registry_rules: Wire capability grant.actions[] entries MUST be drawn from this registry; wildcards / segment globs are statically rejected by capability-grant.schema.json.

Receivers MUST default to risk_tier=high when an action submitted in a grant or evaluated in policy is not present in this registry; this is the freshness fail-closed default required by capabilities.md §18.

required_constraints lists typed-constraint shorthand names that the capability evaluator MUST enforce for the action regardless of the grant author's declarations; absence in this list does NOT disable other declared constraints.

required_evaluator_checks lists non-grant-field invariants (for example actor_eq_target_author or audit_pair_required) that admission control MUST enforce from Event context, reducer state, or paired audit evidence. These are not grant-constraint schema fields.

target_event_kinds links the action to one or more ak.* event_kinds in event_kind_registry. Empty array means the action authorizes a read / projection / signaling path that does not produce a durable reducer-input event. Reducer admission for a listed event_kind MUST verify the actor holds at least one matching action grant.

profile is null for v1 core actions, or a ak.profile.*.v<n> id when the action is only meaningful inside that profile. Receivers without the named profile MUST treat the action as unknown (risk_tier=high default).

Every action MUST declare event_mapping_kind. action == single target_event_kind uses same_name; empty target_event_kinds uses non_event_surface; any other mapping MUST use one of the allowed deviation categories.

actions.notes: Creates an intra-Realm Circle (scoped event/message boundary; optionally MLS-backed depending on parent Realm floor). NOT in default member bundle by default — Circles should be few and stable. See zh/models/circle.md §8.
Manage an existing Circle. MUST be constrained to specific circle_id selectors; unconstrained Realm-wide grant is not a normal management permission.
Self-service: actor accepts an invite, joins a join_rule=open Circle, or leaves. Reducer enforces payload.actor_id == envelope.actor_id and transition legality. Self-unbanning MUST fail closed.
Invite / remove others. Held by Circle admin. payload.actor_id != envelope.actor_id.
Cross-actor write (rare). MUST carry ak.audit.accessed pair (same model as ak.strand.watch.set.others).

Read-only audit access for a Realm admin NOT in the target Circle. MUST be paired with ak.audit.accessed event. Does NOT yield historical decryption keys unless the admin is formally added to the Circle.
Authorizes reading an object's discussion / history events (message timeline, redacted-message metainfo, prior revisions). Read / projection surface only; emits no durable reducer event.

Authorizes adding an audience_mention node such as @all or @here to a Message create/revise. @here maps to audience="strand_engaged" and is not presence-filtered. This is an additional gate: the actor MUST also be authorized for the underlying message create/revise action. Effective Realm/Circle policy MUST allow the audience and declare finite max_recipients/quota before notification fanout.

Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer (ak.realm.set_default_strand event; projects Realm default_strand_id). Same-name discipline. The Realm authz gate is realm-admin: holding ak.realm.admin (aggregate admin coverage) satisfies admission, or grant this specific action directly. Reducer MUST verify the referenced Strand already exists (failed_precondition otherwise). See zh/models/strand-and-message.md default-Strand discovery section.

event_mapping_kind_definitions.same_name: Action maps one-to-one to an identically named durable event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.non_event_surface: Action authorizes read/projection/signaling behavior that does not emit a durable reducer event.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.aggregate_admin: Action intentionally covers a bounded administrative family of event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.polymorphic_object: Action covers the same object-lifecycle verb across multiple object event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.scope_suffix_variant: Action adds actor/scope/role qualifiers while reducer admission targets a shared event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.operation_verb: Action token names an operation/command verb that does not match its target event kind name(s); reducer admission resolves the resulting event kind(s) via target_event_kinds. Literal action matching per the actions[] rule applies; carries no aggregate-admin family semantics.
